I work in a medical billing office and everyone in our office has to be certified as HIPAA compliant. That being said I can honestly say that it doesn't look like these doctors actually violated HIPAA.

HIPAA is complicated, but it basically boils down to this: you cannot discuss private medical information with anyone who a) doesn't already know about it or b) does not have a legitimate need to know. Example of a): Husband has cancer and his wife knows, doctor's office calls with test results and husband is not home, office tells wife so she can pass on the message. 100% O.K. by HIPAA standards because she already knew about the cancer. It gets a little foggier if she didn't know, but I digress. Example of b): The husband goes to a hospital for surgery to have his cancer removed. It's going to be a complicated surgery and will require he stay in the hospital for at least one whole day after the surgery for observation. The hospital has to call the husband's insurance company to have his inpatient (admitted to the hospital overnight) stay authorized, otherwise the insurance will deny the claim and not pay the hospital. This is O.K. with HIPAA because the insurance company needs to know.

Now back to the issue at hand. From what I can tell from the examples in the article, the people complaining about the doctors posted their own private info themselves. The doctors merely commented on it. The doctors are treading on some pretty thin ice but in my educated opinion they have not violated HIPAA. Let me put it to you this way: If a man climbs to the roof of a building and shouts at the top of his lungs to the masses below "I HAVE SYPHILIS!", then one of those people asks the mans doctor if he has syphilis and he says yes, he's in the clear legal-wise.
